Part 1: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage of pilot means and variances

Demo: pilot shrinkage, pilot-selected stratification, and estimate pooling ================ 2026-09-11

This is a working demo of three new pieces added to stratsampling, adapted from the if (FALSE) {} sandbox blocks in R/pilot_functions.R, R/strata_eval_functions.R, and scripts/sim_functions.R. For the full technical derivation of the shrinkage estimators, see scripts/pilot_shrinkage_memo.md – this document only summarizes how the pieces fit together and shows them running.

devtools::load_all( quiet = TRUE )   # picks up the in-development package code
library( tidyverse )

A toy population with one real stratification and one useless covariate

Throughout, strata is the DGP’s real stratification (real between-stratum bias/variance heterogeneity), and X1 is pure noise with no relationship to Yobs/Yhat – included so the demos below have both a “good” and a “bad” candidate stratification to contrast.

set.seed( 42 )
dat <- generate_population( N = 1000, n_strat = 4,
                            strata_config = "unbalanced",
                            tau = 0.5, bias = "moderate",
                            residual_var = "heterogeneous",
                            R2_target = 0.6 )
dat$X1 <- rnorm( nrow(dat) )

We can then make a bunch of possible stratifications:

candidates <- create_stratification_candidates( dat, vars = c("Yhat", "X1", "strata"), Z = "Z" )
length( candidates )
## [1] 24

A small pilot (100 of the 1000 units) is coded; everyone else’s Yobs is treated as not-yet-observed:

dat_full <- dat   # saving full data for sim stuff later on
dat$S <- as.numeric( sample( nrow(dat) ) <= 100 )
dat$Yobs[ dat$S == 0 ] <- NA
table( dat$S, dat$Z )
##    
##       0   1
##   0 447 453
##   1  53  47

estimate_pilot_variances(..., shrink = TRUE) shrinks each cell’s raw pilot mean and variance toward a pooled value, with the amount of shrinkage set by how little pilot data that cell has (see the memo for the full derivation: variances are shrunk first, fully pooled across treatment arms; means are shrunk “hybrid” style – the amount of shrinkage is based on all the strata across all the arms, but each cell is still pulled toward its own arm’s grand mean).

How much shrinkage happens depends entirely on whether the candidate stratification captures real signal. We compare three very different candidates from the same pilot:

  • strata_levels – the true stratification: real between-stratum heterogeneity, so shrinkage should be mild.
  • X1_quintiles – cuts on the useless X1: any apparent between-cell spread here is pure noise, so shrinkage should be aggressive.
  • Yhat_X1_2x2 – crosses the meaningful Yhat with the useless X1: some real signal, diluted by noise and split into smaller cells, so shrinkage should land in between.
three_candidates <- c( "strata_levels", "X1_quintiles", "Yhat_X1_2x2" )

rr_three <- map_dfr( three_candidates, function( cname ) {
    estimate_pilot_variances( dat = NULL,
                              S = dat$S, Z = dat$Z,
                              strata = candidates[[ cname ]],
                              Yobs = dat$Yobs, Yhat = dat$Yhat,
                              shrink = TRUE ) %>%
        mutate( candidate = factor( cname, levels = three_candidates ) )
} )

Point size is scaled to each cell’s full-population stratum size (N.zk), so it’s easy to see when a heavily-shrunk point belongs to a small stratum:

ggplot( rr_three, aes( mean_resid_pilot, mean.alloc, col = as.factor(.Z), size = N.zk ) ) +
    facet_wrap( ~ candidate, nrow = 1 ) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_size_continuous( range = c(1, 6), name = "Stratum size (N.zk)" ) +
    geom_abline( intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 2 ) +
    coord_fixed() + theme_minimal() +
    labs( title = "Mean shrinkage: raw vs shrunk cell means",
          x = "raw mean_resid_pilot", y = "shrunk mean.alloc", col = "Z" )

ggplot( rr_three, aes( var_resid_pilot, var.alloc, col = as.factor(.Z), size = N.zk ) ) +
    facet_wrap( ~ candidate, nrow = 1 ) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_size_continuous( range = c(1, 6), name = "Stratum size (N.zk)" ) +
    geom_abline( intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 2 ) +
    coord_fixed() + theme_minimal() +
    labs( title = "Variance shrinkage: raw vs shrunk cell variances",
          x = "raw var_resid_pilot", y = "shrunk var.alloc", col = "Z" )

Points on the dashed 45-degree line are unshrunk; points pulled off it (toward a flat line, since all cells within a candidate then share close to the same pooled value) show heavy shrinkage. strata_levels should sit closest to the line, X1_quintiles should show the cells nearly collapsing onto a single pooled value (both in the mean and, especially, the variance plot), and Yhat_X1_2x2 should fall in between – the shrinkage machinery is reacting to how much real between-cell signal is actually present, not just applying a fixed discount.

Part 2: Using pilot data to choose a stratification

compare_stratifications_precoding() can now rank candidates two ways:

  • Proxy mode (no Yobs/S): ranks by the spread of stratum-mean Yhat alone – no coding needed, but only a proxy for what actually matters (spread of the residual, Yobs - Yhat).
  • Pilot mode (Yobs + S supplied): ranks by mean_spread_pilot - avg_within_var_pilot, a direct pilot estimate of the between-stratum residual spread net of within-stratum noise – computed via estimate_pilot_variances() internally, so it inherits the shrink argument.
cc_shrink   <- compare_stratifications_precoding( dat, candidates, Z = "Z", Yhat = "Yhat",
                                                  Yobs = dat$Yobs, S = dat$S, shrink = TRUE )
cc_noshrink <- compare_stratifications_precoding( dat, candidates, Z = "Z", Yhat = "Yhat",
                                                  Yobs = dat$Yobs, S = dat$S, shrink = FALSE )
cc_proxy    <- compare_stratifications_precoding( dat, candidates, Z = "Z", Yhat = "Yhat" )

tibble( rank = 1:5,
       pilot_shrink   = cc_shrink$stratification[1:5],
       pilot_noshrink = cc_noshrink$stratification[1:5],
       proxy_only     = cc_proxy$stratification[1:5] )
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##    rank pilot_shrink         pilot_noshrink  proxy_only          
##   <int> <chr>                <chr>           <chr>               
## 1     1 Yhat_strata_3x3      Yhat_strata_3x3 Yhat_quintiles      
## 2     2 Yhat_strata_3x2      Yhat_strata_3x2 Yhat_quartiles      
## 3     3 Yhat_strata_2x3      Yhat_strata_2x3 Yhat_strata_3xlevels
## 4     4 Yhat_strata_2x2      Yhat_strata_2x2 Yhat_strata_3x3     
## 5     5 Yhat_strata_2xlevels strata_levels   Yhat_strata_3x2

With only 100 pilot units split across up to ~10 cells, the shrunk and un-shrunk pilot rankings mostly agree here (both put the Yhat_strata interactions on top), but they need not: with a small pilot, a candidate with a couple of thin cells can get an artificially small or large raw variance by chance and move up or down the un-shrunk ranking in a way shrinkage would have damped out. The proxy-only ranking, having no access to Yobs at all, is a different (weaker) signal again – notice it never gets to see that the Yhat_strata interactions outperform plain Yhat cuts, since that requires the pilot’s actual residuals. Re-knit this document with a different set.seed() above, or a smaller pilot, to see the shrunk/un-shrunk rankings diverge more.

Part 3: Pilot-selected stratification, with precision-weighted pooling

one_iter_pilot_select() puts this together as a two-wave design:

  1. Draw a small SRS pilot; use compare_stratifications_precoding() (pilot mode, shrinkage on by default) to pick the best candidate stratification.
  2. Draw a wave-2 sample of the remaining budget from the full population (not the un-piloted remainder – see the comment above the function for why), stratified on the chosen candidate, both proportionally and with pilot-informed optimal (Neyman) allocation.
  3. Combine the pilot-wave estimate and each wave-2 estimate with combine_estimators() – an inverse-variance (“precision”) weighted pooling of two estimates of the same quantity (see its doc string for the exact formulas, and the note there on the independence assumption).

Note: one_iter_pilot_select() draws its own pilot and wave-2 samples internally, so (unlike Parts 1-2 above, which worked from a single small pre-drawn pilot with Yobs masked outside it) it needs everyone’s real Yobs available – we pass it dat_full, the unmasked snapshot saved above, rather than the dat object from Part 1.

source( "scripts/sim_functions.R" )
set.seed( 2026 )
result <- one_iter_pilot_select( dat_full, n_code = 200, candidates = candidates,
                                 pilot_select_frac = 0.05,
                                 Z = "Z", Yhat = "Yhat", Yobs = "Yobs" )
result %>% select( method, est, SEhat, SE, strat_choice, n_pilot )
##                         method       est     SEhat        SE  strat_choice
## 1       Stratified-PilotSelect 0.3654152 0.2530734 0.2716972 strata_levels
## 2          Optimal-PilotSelect 0.6817672 0.2658350 0.2666485 strata_levels
## 3 Pilot+Stratified-PilotSelect 0.5453291 0.2272252 0.2440313 strata_levels
## 4    Pilot+Optimal-PilotSelect 0.8100495 0.2363269 0.2403534 strata_levels
##   n_pilot
## 1      50
## 2      50
## 3      50
## 4      50

Reading the four rows:

  • Stratified-PilotSelect / Optimal-PilotSelect – the wave-2-only estimates (proportional vs. Neyman-optimal allocation) on the pilot-chosen stratum (strat_choice).
  • Pilot+Stratified-PilotSelect / Pilot+Optimal-PilotSelect – each of those, precision-pooled with the pilot-wave (SRS) estimate via combine_estimators(). Since the pilot here is used only to choose the stratification and is otherwise excluded from the wave-2 draw, the two waves being combined are close to independent draws, which is what combine_estimators()’s pooling formula assumes.

The pooled rows should generally have smaller SEhat than either wave alone – that’s the whole point of pooling two (roughly) independent estimates of the same effect – though see the comment block above one_iter_pilot_select() in scripts/sim_functions.R for the acknowledged caveat: if a wave-2 draw happens to recode a unit already in the pilot, the two waves are not exactly independent, so the pooled SE here is a mild approximation.

Further Information

  • scripts/pilot_shrinkage_memo.md – full derivation of the two-stage empirical-Bayes shrinkage (variances first, fully pooled across arms; means “hybrid”, shared amount-of-shrinkage but arm-specific target), with citations.
  • R/pilot_functions.R – estimate_pilot_variances() and the shrinkage internals; its own if (FALSE) {} sandbox has the source for Part 1 above.
  • R/strata_eval_functions.R – evaluate_stratification_precoding() / compare_stratifications_precoding(); its sandbox has the source for Part 2 above.
  • scripts/sim_functions.R – one_iter_pilot_select() and combine_estimators() (see its doc string for the pooling formulas); its sandbox has the source for Part 3 above.
